title: Crippen atom-type count linear prior
spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with an L1 (median) linear model on the counts of the 110 Crippen atom types, computed with rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs or Crippen.GetAtomContribs, plus the TPSA and MolWt terms. Fit it with sklearn QuantileRegressor(quantile=0.5, alpha=1e-3, solver='highs') on the training fold only and use its predictions as the prior. CatBoost MAE is still fitted to the residual of that prior.

title: Scaffold-held-out early stopping for boosting
spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 90/10 groups by Murcko scaffold, using a deterministic shuffle seeded by seed. Train a LightGBM L1 model with up to 2000 rounds on the 90% part and record the validation MAE curve. Refit on all training data using the best round count scaled by 1.1. This learning-rate schedule chooses the number of boosting rounds without leaking scaffolds.

title: kNN target smoothing as regularisation
spec: Before fitting, replace each training target by a smoothed value: y_tilde_i = (1 - lam) * y_i + lam * mean of y_j over the k=5 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules j != i (binary Morgan radius 2), with lam=0.3. Neighbours are found within the training fold only. Fit the existing OLS prior and CatBoost MAE model on y_tilde, and predict test molecules as usual. This shrinks label noise toward local chemistry without touching the features or the model class.

title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pair counts
spec: Add a hashed count fingerprint of Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pairs (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D with Generate.Gen2DFingerprint, folded to 1024 bins by modulo, counts kept) and concatenate it with the existing featurize() output. Keep the OLS prior, the CatBoost MAE residual model and all other settings unchanged. Only the fingerprint block changes.

title: LightGBM linear-leaf residual model
spec: Keep the OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP and its residual target. Replace the CatBoost MAE residual model with LGBMRegressor(objective='l1', linear_tree=True, linear_lambda=1.0, num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.05, n_estimators=400, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed) on the same CatBoost feature matrix (Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors). Piecewise-linear leaves let the residual vary smoothly with polarity descriptors inside each leaf, which the constant-leaf trees cannot do. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Affine recalibration of inner out-of-fold predictions
spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 4-fold scaffold-grouped inner loop on the training fold to get out-of-fold predictions of the full OLS-plus-CatBoost pipeline. Fit a two-parameter affine map y ~ a + b*pred by minimising MAE (scipy.optimize.minimize on the absolute error, starting from a=0, b=1). Refit the pipeline on all training data and apply the map to the test predictions. This corrects systematic stretch or shrinkage without adding model capacity.

title: Abraham-style solvation linear prior
spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a linear model in Abraham-like solvation terms approximated from RDKit: Crippen logP, TPSA, count of H-bond donors, count of H-bond acceptors, and SMARTS-based counts of strong acid groups and aliphatic amines (the ionisation classes). Fit by OLS on the training fold only. Keep the CatBoost MAE model on the residual exactly as now. The prior captures the physics-based polarity-permeability relationship in a few interpretable terms.

title: Variance-threshold feature pruning
spec: Before fitting the random forest, drop Morgan bit columns that are set in fewer than 3 or more than 97 percent of training molecules. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Removing near-constant bits reduces noise in split selection, so the max_features subsampling is spent on informative features.

title: Similarity-gated fallback to the linear prior
spec: For each test molecule, compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity (binary Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits) to the training molecules. Compute the CatBoost residual correction as now. Then final = OLS prior + g * residual, where g = clip((maxsim - 0.25) / 0.25, 0, 1), so that molecules with no close training analogue fall back to the pure OLS prior and close analogues use the full boosted correction. Set the thresholds once, on the training folds only, and do not tune them per test set.

title: Depth-annealed two-stage boosting
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Fit a CatBoost MAE model with depth 8, learning_rate 0.05 and 300 iterations, then continue training it with init_model and depth 4 for 500 more iterations at learning_rate 0.03 (CatBoost fit with init_model=the first model). The first stage captures high-order interactions among fingerprint bits; the second stage refines with smoother shallow trees. Use seed for random_seed in both stages.

title: Ring-topology and linker descriptors
spec: Append about 8 hand-computed topology features to the featurize() output: number of ring systems (fused ring clusters found from RDKit ring info), size of the largest fused ring system, count of ring-atom bonds shared between rings, number of atoms in the longest acyclic linker between two ring systems (via shortest-path over non-ring atoms), fraction of heavy atoms in rings, and the ratio of rotatable bonds to heavy atoms. Compute all of these from RDKit mol objects with no extra packages. Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost settings unchanged.

title: Average a descriptor-only view with the full-feature view
spec: Train two CatBoost MAE models on the OLS residual. The first uses the existing featurize() output (Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors). The second uses only the RDKit descriptor columns (drop the 2048 fingerprint columns), with the same depth and iteration count but a different random seed offset. Average the two residual predictions with equal weight, then add the OLS prior. This is a fixed-weight two-view average, not a learned stack.

title: Additive depth-1 CatBoost model blended with the depth-6 model
spec: Keep the OLS prior and the residual target. Fit a second CatBoost MAE model with depth=1 (a pure additive, per-feature shape model, i.e. an explainable-boosting-style GAM) on the same features, with about 2000 iterations at lr 0.05. Predict with both the depth-6 model and the depth-1 model and average their residual predictions with equal weight before adding the OLS prior. Use the seed argument for both models. Nothing else changes.

title: ARD Gaussian process on standardised RDKit descriptors
spec: Replace the CatBoost residual model with a Gaussian process regressor from scikit-learn. Select RDKit descriptors with finite values, drop near-constant columns, and standardise them using training statistics only. Use a kernel of ConstantKernel times Matern(nu=2.5) with one length scale per descriptor (ARD) plus WhiteKernel, and fit hyperparameters by marginal likelihood on a random subset of at most 400 training molecules, using n_restarts_optimizer=1 and the seed. Fit the GP to the OLS residual and predict the test residual. Add the OLS prior back. Keep Morgan bits out of this model.

title: Huber and MAE residual blend
spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Fit two CatBoost models on the same residual features: one with loss_function='MAE' (as now) and one with loss_function='Huber:delta=0.5'. Average their test predictions with equal weight. Both use depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 800 iterations and random_seed=seed. The Huber model fits the bulk of the residual distribution more efficiently, while MAE keeps the median target, so the average may combine the two strengths.

title: EState fingerprint and EState atom-type sums
spec: Add a block computed from rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol(m), which returns the 79-bin EState count vector and the 79-bin EState sum vector (use the two returned arrays, both float32). Concatenate these 158 values to the existing feature vector after the Morgan counts and descriptors. EState encodes electronic and topological environment of each heavy atom, which differs from Morgan bit identity. Keep all other settings and the OLS prior unchanged.

title: Cosine learning-rate decay in four CatBoost segments
spec: Keep the OLS prior, the residual target, and the feature set. Train CatBoost MAE in four continued segments with init_model: segment lengths of 300, 300, 300, and 300 iterations, with learning rates set per segment by a cosine decay from 0.08 to 0.01 (lr_k = 0.01 + 0.5*(0.08-0.01)*(1+cos(pi*k/3)) for segment k = 0..3). Build each segment as a fresh CatBoostRegressor loaded from the previous one by init_model, so the total budget is 1200 iterations. Predict with the final model. Note that this is a smooth-decay variant of a step-down schedule, so it is a refinement and not a repeat.

title: Tukey-biweight robust linear prior
spec: Replace the OLS prior with a robust fit. Start with the four-term OLS coefficients (intercept plus TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, MolLogP). Run 10 iteratively reweighted least squares steps: compute residuals r, scale s = 1.4826 * median(|r - median(r)|), weights w = (1 - (r/(4.685 s))^2)^2 clipped to [0,1] for |r|<4.685 s and 0 otherwise, then solve the weighted least squares normal equations. Use the resulting coefficients for the prior, and keep the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged. This down-weights extreme Caco-2 outliers when the linear baseline is estimated.

title: CatBoost random strength and Bayesian bootstrap sweep
spec: Keep the OLS prior, the residual target, and the CatBoost MAE model. Add two regularisers that are not yet in the tried list: random_strength=2.0 (score noise in split selection) and bootstrap_type='Bayesian' with bagging_temperature=1.0 (per-row Bayesian weights). Remove any row or column subsampling settings that are not needed. This is a single configuration change, so run it as-is and compare against the 0.3711 incumbent.

title: Depth-two bagged Huber-and-quantile prior
spec: Replace the OLS prior with the average of three linear priors fit on the training fold: OLS on the four terms, OLS on the four terms plus their pairwise products, and a Huber-loss linear fit (sklearn HuberRegressor, epsilon=1.35) on the four terms. Average the three intercept-and-slope vectors into one prior, then keep the CatBoost MAE residual model unchanged. The aim is a more robust prior whose extrapolation error on unseen scaffolds is damped by averaging over linear forms.

title: Piecewise-linear hinge prior on TPSA and MolLogP fit by MAE
spec: Replace the OLS prior with an MAE-fitted hinge-basis model. For TPSA and MolLogP, build a basis of [x, max(x-k, 0)] for knots k at the 25th, 50th and 75th training percentiles. Add MolWt and NumHDonors linearly. Fit the coefficients with sklearn QuantileRegressor (quantile=0.5, alpha=0) on the training fold. Use its predictions as the prior, and fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the residuals.

title: ARD sparse Bayesian linear prior in place of OLS
spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with sklearn ARDRegression fit on the standardised RDKit descriptor block (about 200 columns) plus the four base features, using the training fold only. ARD drives irrelevant coefficients toward zero automatically, so no hand-picked feature list is needed. Keep the CatBoost MAE model fit on the residuals of this prior, and add the prior back at prediction time.

title: Winsorised standardised descriptor inputs
spec: Before the CatBoost residual fit and the OLS prior, clip each RDKit descriptor column to the 1st and 99th percentile of the training fold, computed per column, then standardise with training-fold means and standard deviations. Apply the same clip bounds and statistics to the test molecules. This limits the influence of extreme descriptor values, such as very large molecules, on the linear prior and on tree splits. Leave the Morgan counts and the target unchanged.

title: Stability-selected descriptor subset for the linear prior
spec: Build the linear prior from a stability-selection step. Draw 50 random half-subsamples of the training fold. In each, fit a LassoCV on standardised RDKit descriptors plus the four base features, and record which coefficients are nonzero. Keep the features selected in at least 60 percent of subsamples, refit an OLS prior on them with the full training fold, and fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the residuals. The selection and refit use only training molecules.

title: Untrained random-weight message-passing embedding
spec: Build a graph per molecule (atoms as nodes with a one-hot of element, degree, aromaticity and H-count; bonds as edges with a bond-type one-hot). Run 3 rounds of fixed, random-normal (seeded) message passing in numpy: each node sums its neighbours' features through a random 16x16 matrix followed by tanh, then sum-pools each round. Concatenate the pooled 48-dim vector to the existing features. No training of the embedding is done; it is a random-feature graph embedding.

title: Polynomial LassoCV prior instead of OLS
spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a sparse polynomial prior. Build a design matrix from TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, MolLogP, their squares, and all pairwise products (14 columns in total, standardised using training-fold mean and sd). Fit sklearn LassoCV(cv=5, random_state=seed) on the training fold, then fit the residual CatBoost MAE model exactly as now. Predict the test prior with the same standardisation. The sparse fit lets the prior capture curvature without the overfitting of a dense spline or kernel prior.

title: Stratified target-bin bagging of CatBoost
spec: Split the training fold into 5 bins by quantile of the OLS residual. Train 5 CatBoost MAE models, each on a bootstrap that draws the same fraction of rows from every bin (stratified bagging), using a different seed. Average their test predictions and add the OLS prior back. Stratification keeps the tails of the residual distribution represented in every bag, which ordinary random bootstrap can drop. Keep depth, learning rate and iterations at the current values.

title: Median offset correction after an RMSE residual fit
spec: Keep the OLS prior. Replace the CatBoost MAE residual model with a CatBoost RMSE model (same depth, learning rate, and iterations) fitted to the residual target. Estimate the median bias with 4-fold scaffold-grouped (GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings) out-of-fold predictions on the training fold: compute m = median(residual_true - oof_pred) and add m to the test predictions. This turns a mean-fitted booster into a median-consistent predictor at low cost, without the slower MAE gradient. Use seed for all randomness.

title: Cauchy redescending loss for the residual boosting
spec: Replace the MAE loss of the residual CatBoost model with a custom redescending Cauchy objective implemented as a CatBoost UserDefinedLoss, or use an equivalent two-pass scheme: first fit the current MAE model, then compute residuals and reweight training rows by w = 1/(1 + (res/c)^2) with c set to 1.4826 times the median absolute residual, and refit CatBoost with RMSE on the reweighted rows. Use the same features, OLS prior and iterations. The redescending weight ignores the largest outliers entirely rather than only down-weighting them linearly as MAE does.

title: Multi-conformer averaged three-dimensional descriptors
spec: Extend the 3D descriptor block by generating 10 ETKDG conformers per molecule with a fixed seed (rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3, randomSeed=seed, numConfs=10), MMFF-optimise each, and compute PBF, PMI1-3, NPR1-2 and radius of gyration per conformer. Append the mean and standard deviation over conformers to the feature matrix. Fall back to 2D-only features for any molecule where embedding fails. Use the same CatBoost MAE residual setup.

title: BRICS fragment count block appended to features
spec: Keep the current featurize() (Morgan radius-2 counts, 2048 bits, plus RDKit descriptors) and the OLS prior with CatBoost MAE on the residual. Append a 512-bin hashed count vector of BRICS fragments: for each molecule call BRICS.BRICSDecompose(mol) to get fragment SMILES, convert each with Chem.MolFromSmiles, take the canonical SMILES, and hash it with a stable hash (e.g. zlib.crc32 modulo 512) into a count vector. Fragment counts are a chemically different substructure view from Morgan environments. Use np.float32 and nan_to_num as before. No other changes.

title: Avalon count fingerprint replacing Morgan counts
spec: In featurize(), replace the Morgan count block with Avalon count fingerprints from rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(m, nBits=1024), converted to a dense float32 array via GetNonzeroElements. Avalon hashes path-based and ring-aware features and is not in the tried list. Keep the RDKit descriptor block, the four-term OLS prior, and CatBoost MAE on the residual. Do not add any other fingerprint.

title: Test-time averaging over featurisation variants
spec: Build three feature variants of each molecule: Morgan count fingerprint at radius 2 with chirality off, the same at radius 2 with useChirality=True, and the radius-3 Morgan count version, each with its own 2048-bin hashing. Train the same CatBoost MAE residual model on the training molecules once per variant (with the same OLS prior), and average the three test predictions with equal weight. The variants differ only in how the local environment is encoded, so the average reduces variance from any single hashing or stereo choice.

title: Pairwise interaction features among the top polarity descriptors
spec: Choose the six RDKit descriptors with the highest absolute Spearman correlation to the OLS residual on the training fold. Form all 15 pairwise products and the 15 pairwise ratios with a small epsilon in the denominator, and append these 30 columns to the existing feature matrix. Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model. Compute the chosen descriptor set inside fit_predict using only training molecules so that no test information leaks.

title: Descriptor-space k-nearest-neighbour median blended with CatBoost
spec: Compute standardised RDKit descriptors (from Descriptors.descList, winsorised at the training-fold 1st and 99th percentiles and standardised with training-fold mean and sd). For each test molecule, take the k=15 nearest training molecules in this standardised space (Euclidean) and compute the median of their OLS residuals. Blend this kNN residual estimate with the CatBoost residual prediction using a fixed weight of 0.25 on kNN and 0.75 on CatBoost, then add the OLS term. This is a non-parametric second view with a different inductive bias from trees.

title: Intramolecular hydrogen-bond and shielded-polarity counts
spec: Append a small block of about six SMARTS-based counts to the existing features. Count polar groups that are likely masked by an intramolecular hydrogen bond: amide or carboxamide NH groups with an acceptor on the adjacent atom, phenol OH ortho to a carbonyl or nitrogen, and NH-to-carbonyl pairs separated by one or two bonds. Also count the total polar atoms that are not masked. Concatenate these to the descriptor vector and keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. These features target the known chameleonic behaviour that drives Caco-2 permeability beyond raw TPSA.

title: Backfitted MAE additive spline model before the residual CatBoost
spec: Replace the OLS prior with a generalised additive model. Expand TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors and RotatableBonds into a cubic B-spline basis with 5 knots each. Fit the additive model by backfitting: cycle over the features, and for each feature fit a 1-D smoothing spline to the partial residual under a Huber-like robust loss, for 10 cycles. Use the resulting additive prediction as the prior. Fit the existing CatBoost MAE model on the residual, and add the prior back at prediction time. The change is limited to the prior.

title: Langevin (SGLB) CatBoost residual model
spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model. Add langevin=True and diffusion_temperature=1000 to the CatBoostRegressor constructor, and remove any bootstrap option so the posterior-style noise is the only stochasticity. Leave depth, learning rate, iterations and seed unchanged. The only change is the optimiser: noisy gradient Langevin boosting, which regularises leaf values through injected noise rather than through subsampling.

title: Heteroatom topological-distance pair histogram
spec: Append a compact histogram of topological distances between heteroatom pairs (N, O, F, Cl, S, P, Br), computed with Chem.GetDistanceMatrix on each molecule. Count pairs for distances 1 to 12 with distances above 12 pooled into one bin, separately for pair classes N-N, N-O, O-O, and hetero-to-carbon, giving about 48 integer columns. Fit no transform, use float32, and concatenate with the existing featurize() output. Heteroatom spacing is the topology that drives hydrogen-bond and polarity effects in permeability, and it is not in Morgan counts or the RDKit descriptor list.

title: DART-style LightGBM L1 residual model
spec: Replace the CatBoost residual model with LightGBM in DART mode (boosting_type='dart', objective='l1', drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, about 400 rounds, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, feature_fraction 0.5, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1). Fit it on the same OLS-prior residual target and use the seed as random_state. DART's tree dropout is a different regulariser from CatBoost's, and it targets the overfitting on rare fingerprint bits that the family-swap trials did not address.

title: Quantile regression forest conditional median on the residual
spec: After the OLS prior, fit a sklearn RandomForestRegressor (300 trees, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=0.3, random_state=seed) on the residual using featurize() columns. At prediction time, do not use the forest mean: for each test molecule, collect the training residuals that share a leaf with it across all trees, weight each by 1/(leaf size) summed over trees, and take the weighted median as the residual prediction. This gives a conditional-median estimate matched to the MAE metric. Implement with apply() on train and test, and keep it vectorised.

title: Pairwise difference learning with nearest-neighbour anchors
spec: For each test molecule, find its k=10 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto on binary Morgan radius-2 fingerprints. Build training pairs (i, j) from training molecules and their 10 nearest training neighbours, with target d_ij = y_i - y_j and features [x_i, x_j, x_i - x_j] using the existing descriptors and fingerprints. Fit one CatBoost regressor (MAE loss, depth 6, 800 iterations) on the pairs. For a test molecule t, predict y_t as the mean over its 10 anchors j of (y_j + f(x_t, x_j, x_t - x_j)). Subsample pairs to at most 30000 for the 6 GB and 10 minute limits. This turns a regression into local analogical differences and can reduce bias on molecules in sparse regions.
